The fund includes a R240 million commitment from the Development Bank of Southern Africa as lead development finance institution.

Initial investments will target commercial and industrial solar and storage projects across Africa and the Indian Ocean islands.

The investment pipeline also covers generation, transmission related infrastructure, water and gas assets.

Airnergize Capital, the clean technology investment platform of New GX Capital, has reached the final close of its first fund at R3.89 billion.

The Development Bank of Southern Africa committed R240 million to the fund as its lead development finance institution investor. The commitment followed a full institutional assessment of Airnergize Capital’s platform, governance structures and investment process.

Airnergize Capital invests institutional and development capital in energy, water and gas infrastructure businesses across Southern Africa and other African markets. The platform is black owned and controlled, with a mandate to deliver measurable environmental and social outcomes alongside commercial returns.

The Fund I investor group includes New GX Capital, RMB Ventures, Standard Bank, Nedbank and the DBSA. The structure brings together several of South Africa’s largest commercial financial institutions and its development finance institution in a single investment vehicle.

Initial capital deployment will focus on commercial and industrial solar and energy storage assets in South Africa, sub–Saharan Africa and the Indian Ocean islands. The fund also has a broader pipeline covering power generation, transmission related infrastructure, water and gas projects.

Author: Bryan Groenendaal
